Laboratory Report 1: Microscopy and Measurement. Convert ocular divisions to micrometers using 10 ocular divisions = 25 micrometers. Calculate cell length for 12 cells and report mean, range, and sample size for each tissue. Create a plot showing every measurement. Evaluate whether field selection or cell orientation could bias the observed difference. Focus on estimation, variation, and measurement limitations.

Applied Cognition Note 4: Retrieval Practice. Compare rereading with retrieval practice using two equally difficult sets of course terms. Study one set by rereading and one by closed-book retrieval plus feedback. After a 24-hour delay, define the terms without notes. Explain the result using retrieval strength, feedback, and metacognitive fluency, while acknowledging that one participant cannot establish general effectiveness.

Digital Exhibit Proposal. Define a narrow, researchable historical question for a six-item public-facing exhibit. Specify the date range, geography, intended audience, and why the question matters. Identify plausible item types and preliminary citations. Explain a provisional argument and how evidence could complicate it. Identify an ethical, rights, representation, or accessibility issue and a plan for addressing it.
